chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said:

If the matter were up to us, we would permit the testimony of one man, if goodness is known of him, along with the oath of the claimant, in the rights of people. But as for what is from the rights of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the sighting of the crescent moon, then no.

key_terms.حُقُوقِ ٱللَّهِ: matters classified as the rights of Allah
key_terms.حُقُوقِ ٱلنَّاسِ: private rights and claims belonging to people
key_terms.خَيْرٌ: known uprightness or goodness in the witness
key_terms.رُؤْيَةِ ٱلْهِلَالِ: the sighting of the new crescent moon for legal-religious purposes
key_terms.يَمِينِ: a formal oath used in judicial procedure
key_terms.ٱلْخَصْمِ: the litigant or claimant in the case

ai.seo_question: Can one witness and the claimant’s oath establish a case in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses a legal distinction between private human claims and matters regarded as the rights of Allah. It indicates that in the rights of people, one upright man’s testimony together with the claimant’s oath could be accepted, whereas this would not apply to Allah’s rights or to crescent sighting.
